tasks.short: Prepare and deliver political science lectures

steps.what: Read political thought and empirical sources and choose the argument, learning aims and examples for the lecture

Prepare lectures on political thought, international relations or democracy in {DOCS}; write actual explanations and check the completed slides while native layouts reuse headings and reference formatting
Publish the exact checked lecture material to the checked course audience in {LMS}
Deliver the lecture and respond to undergraduate or graduate students' questions about the political arguments and evidence

tasks.design: Test native slide layouts and reference styles in {DOCS}. Reuse format while the teacher chooses and explains political arguments, checks the final material and course audience, publishes it and teaches the class.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated lecture layout and reference formatting can take time.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document styles can reuse structure without selecting political claims.
tasks.still_hard: Representing contested ideas fairly and answering students requires scholarly judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher distinguishes an argument's assumptions from evidence for it.

ambition.what: No expanded teaching or assessment authority.

tasks.altitude: Less formatting; unchanged preparation and teaching judgement.

reach.task: Align learning activities with course aims
reach.learn: Check whether an example teaches an argument rather than a partisan conclusion.

evidence.claim: Native layouts and reference styles can reduce repeated lecture formatting.

assumptions: Boundary is lecture preparation, material release and delivery, not grading or separately assessed discussion. No student or other-role labour saving is credited.

The teacher produces learning aims, source identifiers, actual claims, examples and slide sequence in s1-s2. Existing course records supply audience and template. Missing references are resolved manually; source reading and factual review stay counted.

Native configuration first. Shares are illustrative, not measured baselines. Final s2 checking follows completed material and includes course audience and rights; changed content or destination voids the release check.
unknowns: Whether layouts already remove repeat formatting
research_questions: Which repeated formatting remains after native styles are used?

already_counted.description: Actual lecture writing and final checking remain in s2.

incremental.description: Maintain course layout and reference styles.

approvals.approved_version: Completed lecture material and course audience checked in s2; edits require rechecking.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Repeated layout gives 6 gross hours less 1 upkeep for 5 net. Existing layouts give zero gain. Source judgement, actual delivery and release effort remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Keep abreast of political science developments by locating and reading current literature, examining methods and comparing competing arguments
Talk with colleagues about current findings, disputed interpretations and methods
Participate in professional conferences and discuss political science research with presenters and peers
Write and check actual reading and conference notes and source pointers in {DOCS}
Save the exact checked scholarly notes in {DOCS}

tasks.design: Keep current-source reading, scholarly conversation, conference participation and actual notes unchanged. Existing {DOCS} search and reference tools are assumed to be in ordinary use; no duplicated capture is established.
tasks.previous_blocker: Understanding new political science depends on reading methods and debating interpretations.
tasks.enabler_now: No further time-saving mechanism is established beyond existing native tools.
tasks.still_hard: A source summary cannot settle the strength of a causal argument.
tasks.human_edge: The scholar recognises theoretical differences and methodological limitations.

reach.learn: Use source provenance and subject indexing effectively.

evidence.claim: Scholarly evaluation requires direct attention to arguments and methods, beyond bibliographic retrieval.

assumptions: Boundary is keeping current, including ordinary personal notes, not producing a formal literature review or administering conference travel. Actual note writing and saving are split from conversation and participation and retain their effort.

Publishers and conference organisers supply actual papers, author, date and session details. The teacher selects and reads them in s1-s3 and captures actual understanding in s4. Missing sources are found manually; no free structured synthesis is assumed.

Illustrative shares are not measured. Native search and note capture already operate; no new tool or configuration is proposed, hence zero upkeep. The ordinary final s4 note check binds the completed version before saving.
unknowns: Whether any real duplicate note capture occurs
research_questions: Do native search tools leave a demonstrated navigation problem?

already_counted.description: Actual scholarly notes and checking remain in s4.

incremental.description: No new tool or procedure; zero additional upkeep.

approvals.approved_version: Actual scholarly notes checked in s4; any edit voids the check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Literature reading, dialogue, conference work, notes and saving are separately considered and unchanged; no new administrative baseline or saving is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Evaluate and grade political science work

steps.what: Read students' class work, assignments and papers and evaluate political arguments, evidence, methods and attribution against the published rubric
Determine rubric scores and grade students' work in {LMS}; enter actual judgements while native weighting calculates the numerical total
Write individual feedback and check the completed grade, weighting, evidence and student identity before recording or releasing the final result
Commit the exact checked grade and feedback in {LMS}
Release the exact recorded grade and feedback to the checked student through {LMS}

tasks.design: Test native rubric weighting in {LMS}. The examiner reads the work, determines every score, writes individual feedback and checks the final student-bound result before separately committing and releasing it; no model grades the student.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual rubric addition can repeat arithmetic after academic judgement is complete.
tasks.enabler_now: Native weight formulas can calculate totals from teacher-entered scores.
tasks.still_hard: Strong political argument cannot be inferred from keyword or citation counts.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher assesses the student's reasoning fairly across competing political positions.
tasks.altitude: A small reduction in score arithmetic, unchanged examiner judgement.

reach.learn: Test rounding and weighting against the published assessment rules.

evidence.claim: Native rubric weighting can total teacher-entered marks without assessing the student's reasoning.

assumptions: Boundary is the appointed examiner's assessment and normal result release, excluding appeals and examination-board decisions. No automated grading or misconduct inference is proposed.

The course team supplies published criterion IDs, weights and rounding rules. The examiner supplies actual criterion scores and student ID in s1-s2; entry time is counted. Missing work or ambiguous rubric rules require manual handling.

Native configuration first. Shares are illustrative, not measured baselines. The completed final grade and feedback exist before the ordinary s3 check, which binds the exact student and visibility; any edit voids both commit and release approvals.
unknowns: Whether a separate student-record system requires a confirmed second entry
research_questions: Is manual rubric arithmetic a real part of present marking?

already_counted.description: Score judgement, arithmetic review and final individual feedback remain in s2-s3.

incremental.description: Check rubric formula and rounding when course rules change.

approvals.approved_version: Final grade, feedback and student identity checked in s3; any edit voids approval.
Same final result checked in s3 and committed unchanged in s4, to the exact checked student audience.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only repeated score arithmetic changes: 3 gross less 0.5 upkeep gives 2.5 net. Existing native weighting gives no new saving. Reading, judgement, feedback and result actions keep their effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Choose the political question, source passages and discussion ground rules for the class
Initiate, facilitate and moderate classroom discussions, invite reasoned disagreement and respond to students' actual contributions
Write and check the actual follow-up explanation of unresolved concepts in the existing {LMS} course item
Post the exact checked follow-up explanation to the checked course audience in {LMS}

tasks.design: Keep the discussion and actual follow-up explanation in the existing {LMS} workflow. After separating the written output and posting, no repeated record entry or safe substitute for the teacher's response is established.
tasks.previous_blocker: Moderation depends on what students actually say and understand.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing course items already support follow-up; no additional change is demonstrated.
tasks.still_hard: Contentious subjects need fair participation and real-time scholarly judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher can challenge reasoning without suppressing legitimate disagreement.

reach.learn: Distinguish balanced participation from forced agreement.

evidence.claim: Discussion moderation requires responding to actual student reasoning.

assumptions: Boundary is discussion planning, live moderation and a short ordinary course follow-up, not transcript production, student profiling or grading. This scenario assumes existing follow-up practice; it does not claim every class produces a report.

The teacher selects the question and source passages in s1, obtains actual contributions in s2 and writes the explanation in s3. No recording or extraction supplies free structured discussion data. Missing context is clarified directly.

Shares are illustrative, not measured. Native course entry already works, and no duplicate capture is established. Ordinary final s3 checking binds the completed explanation and course audience before posting; any edit voids the check. No new tool means zero upkeep.
unknowns: Whether a normal course follow-up is part of local practice
research_questions: Is any actual duplicated follow-up work present beyond native course entry?

already_counted.description: Actual follow-up writing and checking remain in s3.

incremental.description: No new tool or procedure; zero additional upkeep.

approvals.approved_version: Final explanation and course audience checked in s3; edits require rechecking.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Planning, live moderation, actual follow-up and posting are separately counted and unchanged. No extra reporting baseline or automated understanding of political views is assumed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Formatting and arithmetic may shrink; scholarly reading, teaching and assessment remain human.
reach: Work with assessment and instructional coordinators on native course rules.
role.ambitious_version: A political science teacher whose systems handle repeated formats while academic judgement remains explicit.
